newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB to issue 386.4 mln preferred shares.
newsitem.headline: NCB to issue 386.4 mln preferred shares.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) said on Monday it would issue 386.40 million preferred stocks worth 123.65 billion yen.
The price of a single share will be 320 yen and the payment date is July 28, NCB said in a statement.
A special fund set up by the Japanese government will purchase 250 million of the preferred shares, making it the largest buyer of shares, NCB said.
The fund is designed to deal with bad loans at failed housing loan firms, or "jusen".

Among the 21 other buyers, all of which are life and non-life insurers, the top buyer will be Sumitomo Life Insurance Co with 35.16 million shares, followed by Mitsui Mutual Life Insurance Co which will buy 18.75 million shares, NCB said.
Asahi Mutual Life Insurance Co and Toho Mutual Life Insurance Co will buy 11.72 million shares each and Nippon Life Insurance Co will buy 10.16 million shares, NCB said.

NCB, one of Japan's three long-term credit banks, unveiled a radical restructuring plan in April supported by the Finance Ministry under which it said it would aggressively write off problem loans and retreat from overseas operations. It said it was selling prime real estate and floating new shares to try to rebuild its capital base.
